engineering_complete_node_0: A visitor supplies the information needed to create an account.
engineering_complete_node_1: Required fields and the email format are valid. The interface can continue.
engineering_complete_node_2: Confirm the action clearly and explain what the person can do next.
engineering_missing_node_0: A visitor tries to continue before all required details are present.
engineering_missing_node_1: Stop at the relevant field. Identify what is missing without losing the other input.
engineering_missing_node_2: Give a specific correction and keep the person in the same flow.
engineering_existing_node_0: A visitor tries to register with an email that already belongs to an account.
engineering_existing_node_1: Treat the conflict as a recoverable situation and avoid unnecessary disclosure.
engineering_existing_node_2: Offer a safe route to sign in or recover access instead of a dead end.

engineering_missing_response: Check the required details. Keep the information already entered.
engineering_existing_response: Guide the person toward sign-in or account recovery.

engineering_detail_2_title: Feedback is part of the workflow.

engineering_principle_1: Simple interfaces still need thoughtful rules.
engineering_principle_3: A good solution starts with understanding the problem.

bsa_jomgo_title: JomGo — Public Transport System Case Study
bsa_jomgo_desc: Exploring a clearer journey through Klang Valley public transport: route comparison, fare estimates, live bus data, and GPS trip tracking.
bsa_evidence_note: Evidence boundary: this is a retrospective analysis of the JomGo-web source at commit 0757591. Requirements, priorities, stakeholder needs, and UAT scenarios were reconstructed for this portfolio. They are not records of client discovery or formal UAT. “Implemented” means present in inspected code, not independently validated in production.
bsa_role_body: A personal transit project with frontend and integration work visible in its source. This portfolio adds the analytical artifacts below. The app uses Lovable/TanStack scaffolding and third-party libraries; this review does not establish sole authorship of every module.
bsa_evidence_intro: Start with a question. Follow it to an artifact, the implementation, and a way to verify it.
bsa_status_note: No items are marked in progress or planned: no delivery commitment was established by this review. Proposed items are recommendations.
bsa_problem_body: A commuter may need to combine route, fare, and journey-status information before deciding how to travel. JomGo explores bringing those decisions into one mobile experience.
bsa_affected_body: People planning supported Klang Valley journeys, especially when comparing a transfer, a fare, or an unfamiliar stop. These needs have not been validated through interviews here.
bsa_why_body: Searching and interpreting separate information could add cognitive effort. No baseline, user sample, or measured time saving is available.
bsa_opportunity_body: Connect station selection, route comparison, and trip tracking. Make the limits of estimates and external data visible.
bsa_observation_body: The source separates route search, fare estimation, a live map, and active-trip tracking.
bsa_assumption_body: A combined experience may help commuters make journey decisions with less switching between tools.
bsa_evidence_body: search.tsx invokes the planner; trip.tsx consumes the saved route; use-vehicle-positions.ts polls external bus feeds.
bsa_requirement_body: FR-01: compare supported origin–destination options before starting a trip.
bsa_solution_body: A route-selection interface connected to planning logic, a local trip store, and a map.
bsa_stakeholders_note: Inferred stakeholder map. No stakeholder interviews or influence scores are claimed. Data providers are dependencies, not project sponsors.
bsa_process_note: Illustrative comparison, not a measured before-and-after study. Intended improvement: fewer context switches between planning and tracking.
bsa_catalog_note: Retrospective requirements derived from inspected behavior and identified gaps. Expand a requirement for rationale, source, and verification links.
bsa_functional_body: Select stations, compare route options, start a trip, and display available bus positions.
bsa_nonfunctional_body: Remain usable on mobile, show trustworthy data states, and handle permission or service failures. Source presence is not proof that these qualities have been validated.
bsa_moscow_note: A retrospective MoSCoW proposal for the core planning journey. Priority does not imply delivery status.
bsa_must_body: FR-01 + DR-01: supported stations and route comparison are prerequisites for making a journey choice. NFR-02 is a proposed reliability gate: empty data must not imply a healthy service.
bsa_should_body: FR-02 + FR-03 + IR-01: trip continuity and live context add value after a route can be selected; planning can still operate without GPS or a live feed.
bsa_could_body: FR-04: community crowding reports may add context, but require moderation, freshness rules, and validation before implementation.
bsa_wont_body: Ticket purchasing, guaranteed arrival predictions, and nationwide transit coverage are outside this portfolio’s current analysis scope.
bsa_rules_note: A requirement describes a capability; a rule constrains its behavior; the UI presents it. These rules are reconstructed from source.
bsa_context_note: Inside the boundary: JomGo client, planning logic, local storage, and its deployed server handlers. Outside: commuters, device services, data providers, map tiles, and optional account services.
bsa_architecture_note: The core transit path runs in the browser. Server handlers support other integrations; Supabase is optional for account data. This is not a mandatory client → Worker → database pipeline.
bsa_dataflow_note: Current limitation: fetchFeedVehicles returns success:false on failure, but fetchAllVehicles flattens vehicle arrays and drops that status. An outage can look like an empty feed. NFR-02 proposes preserving partial errors and freshness.
bsa_uat_title: UAT design / ready to execute, not claimed as passed
bsa_uat_note: All scenarios below are unexecuted designs. Reviewing source is not UAT. Portfolio regression tests validate this website, not JomGo’s production behavior.
bsa_lifecycle_title: From a need to a testable outcome.
bsa_lifecycle_note: Select a journey, then hover, focus, or tap any node to inspect the connected path. Every chain ends in a verification design and expected value, not a claimed result.
bsa_decisions_note: Implementation choices are observable in code; the explanations and alternatives below are retrospective analysis, not an original decision-meeting record.
bsa_inscope_body: Supported station selection; route/fare comparison; active-trip persistence; GPS tracking; available bus positions. Optional profile/history integration is configuration-dependent.
bsa_value_note: No production KPI, revenue result, or measured travel-time improvement is claimed. The next step is to test whether the delivered features improve real journey decisions.
bsa_learning_body: A connected interface is only part of a reliable journey. Estimates need honest labels; an empty result needs a reason; a feature needs a traceable acceptance check. The next validation should observe commuters comparing routes and test feed failures on real devices.
bsa_cap_analysis_body: Problem framing, As-Is / To-Be, gap analysis, requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria — explored through JomGo artifacts.
bsa_cap_systems_body: Trace browser, API, data, and optional persistence paths. Explain dependencies, validation, failure states, and technical trade-offs.
bsa_cap_delivery_body: Frontend implementation and documented ERP QA/UAT experience, connected to proposed acceptance checks and requirement traceability.
bsa_cap_tools_body: React, JavaScript, TypeScript, PHP, Git, Vite, REST APIs, and Supabase integration are represented in the documented projects.
bsa_short_note: A concise retrospective walkthrough based on the existing project description and assets. Acceptance checks are proposed; no new user research or executed UAT is claimed.
bsa_overview_systems: System, API & data → follow the connections
bsa_commuter_need: Compare a supported journey and follow the selected trip.
bsa_commuter_pain: Unfamiliar transfers or uncertainty about the next stop.
bsa_provider_need: A client that handles feed formats and missing data.
bsa_provider_pain: Schema changes, unavailable feeds, or stale positions.
bsa_provider_interaction: Publishes static GTFS and realtime protobuf feeds.
bsa_maintainer_need: Understand data paths, deployment, and failure modes.
bsa_maintainer_pain: Silent failures or configuration-dependent account features.
bsa_maintainer_interaction: Maintains adapters, builds, and optional service configuration.
bsa_contributor_need: Share useful crowding context if a reporting feature is validated.
bsa_contributor_pain: Reports could be stale or unreliable.
bsa_contributor_interaction: No reporting flow observed; FR-04 is proposed.
bsa_tobe_3: Start trip / review map & bus feed
bsa_gap1_current: Route and fare information may require separate checks.
bsa_gap1_response: Route cards show time, transfers, and estimated fares. FR-01.
bsa_gap2_current: Remembering an unfamiliar destination can be difficult (assumption).
bsa_gap2_gap: Planning does not itself support trip execution.
bsa_gap2_desired: Keep the chosen trip available while travelling.
bsa_gap2_response: Saved trip, GPS view, and device-dependent arrival cue. FR-02 / FR-03.
bsa_gap3_current: Feed failure is flattened to an empty vehicle list in code.
bsa_gap3_gap: No-data and unavailable-service states can be conflated.
bsa_gap3_desired: Know when live information cannot be trusted.
bsa_gap3_response: Preserve per-feed error and freshness metadata. NFR-02.
bsa_gap4_current: The planner has an estimated straight-line fallback.
bsa_gap4_gap: A fallback can be mistaken for a verified itinerary.
bsa_gap4_desired: Distinguish approximation from a supported connection.
bsa_gap4_response: Add explicit estimate / unsupported-connection labels. NFR-02.
bsa_BR-01_description: Support informed journey decisions across supported Klang Valley transit options.
bsa_BR-01_reason: Product hypothesis, not a measured business result.
bsa_FR-01_description: Compare supported origin–destination plans by estimated time, fare, and transfers.
bsa_FR-01_reason: search.tsx invokes planRoutes and labelPlans; number of alternatives depends on the network.
bsa_FR-02_description: Persist a selected trip and open it in the active-trip view.
bsa_FR-02_reason: Search saves the selected plan to the local trip store before navigation.
bsa_FR-03_description: Use GPS during an active trip and trigger a proximity cue when the configured threshold is reached.
bsa_FR-03_reason: Device permissions and sound/vibration capabilities are dependencies; delivery is not guaranteed.
bsa_IR-01_description: Decode available live bus feeds and expose normalized positions to the map.
bsa_IR-01_reason: Direct CORS fetch, protobuf decoding, and finite-coordinate filtering in the hook.
bsa_DR-01_description: Represent supported stops with an ID, name, coordinates, mode, and line membership.
bsa_DR-01_reason: GTFS ZIP stops are parsed and normalized before planning.
bsa_NFR-01_description: Provide responsive layouts for station selection and trip review.
bsa_NFR-01_reason: Responsive app shell and layouts exist; real-device usability validation remains open.
bsa_NFR-02_description: Distinguish unavailable, empty, stale, and estimated data without implying live certainty.
bsa_NFR-02_reason: Current feed aggregation loses errors; planner fallback estimates require clear labeling.
bsa_FR-04_description: Explore community crowding reports with explicit moderation and freshness rules.
bsa_FR-04_reason: Crowd-sourced indicators appear in README roadmap; no submission implementation was observed.
bsa_US-01_body: As a commuter, I want to compare supported routes so that I can choose a suitable balance of travel time, fare, and transfers.
bsa_US-01_given: Two distinct supported stations are loaded.
bsa_US-01_when: I select an origin and destination.
bsa_US-01_then: Available plans display estimated duration, fare, and transfers; the same plan may carry more than one comparison label.
bsa_US-02_body: As a commuter, I want available bus positions on the map so that I can add current context to my journey decision.
bsa_US-02_given: A supported feed returns decodable vehicles with finite coordinates.
bsa_US-02_when: The map consumes the vehicle query.
bsa_US-02_then: Valid records become map markers. Feed failure messaging is a separate proposed criterion under NFR-02.
bsa_US-03_body: As a commuter, I want my selected route available during a trip so that I can follow the destination and next steps.
bsa_US-03_given: A supported plan is selected and browser storage is available.
bsa_US-03_when: I start the trip and open the trip view.
bsa_US-03_then: The destination and selected plan are restored. GPS-dependent information additionally requires location permission.
bsa_RULE-01_description: Missing, identical, or unknown station IDs produce no plan; the initial search prompt is not a specialized error message.
bsa_RULE-02_description: Fastest, cheapest, and fewest-transfer labels are computed over returned candidates; a route can win several labels.
bsa_RULE-03_description: A proximity cue fires once per active alert state when distance is within the configured threshold; device support still applies.
bsa_actor1_body: Station choices → route options / trip feedback
bsa_actor2_body: Location permission & coordinates ↔ GPS and arrival cues
bsa_actor3_body: Static GTFS + live bus positions → client adapters
bsa_actor5_body: Supabase Auth / profiles / history ↔ client SDK
bsa_layer1_body: Station selection and route cards connect user intent to planner outputs. TanStack Query manages data fetching.
bsa_layer2_body: Graph-based candidates, fare estimation, and localStorage support comparison and continuity without mandatory account storage.
bsa_layer3_body: Browser → data.gov.my for station ZIPs and live bus protobuf → normalized records → Leaflet. CORS and provider availability are dependencies.
bsa_layer4_body: Cloudflare Pages / Nitro serves the app; news has a same-origin handler. Live bus fetching does not require that proxy.
bsa_layer5_body: The browser SDK supports account profiles and history when configured; local history is a fallback. Deployed RLS policies were not audited.
bsa_api1_title: Live bus feed / direct browser integration
bsa_api1_input: Agency + supported bus category; polling through TanStack Query.
bsa_api1_output: Decoded vehicle IDs, coordinates, optional timestamps → map markers.
bsa_api1_validation: HTTP response check, protobuf decode, and finite coordinates.
bsa_api1_failure: Adapter returns failure metadata; aggregation currently drops it. NFR-02 proposes preserving it.
bsa_api1_dependency: Provider uptime, CORS, protobuf schema, network connection.
bsa_api2_input: Rail and bus GTFS ZIP feeds.
bsa_api2_output: Normalized stop IDs, names, positions, modes, and lines → planner.
bsa_api2_validation: ZIP and stops.txt parsing; non-finite coordinates are skipped.
bsa_api2_failure: A failed feed becomes an empty list; distinguish partial coverage before trusting a plan (proposed).
bsa_api2_dependency: External static feed and station/line mapping.
bsa_UAT-01_expected: Available candidate cards show estimated time/fare/transfers; labels match candidate comparisons.
bsa_UAT-02_scenario: Supply a valid feed containing valid and non-finite coordinates.
bsa_UAT-02_expected: Only finite-coordinate records reach the map. Check decoded identity and position.
bsa_UAT-03_scenario: Start a selected trip, then revisit the trip view with storage enabled.
bsa_UAT-03_expected: Destination and selected route persist; an absent trip displays the empty-trip state.
bsa_UAT-04_scenario: Simulate location updates outside and inside the configured alert distance.
bsa_UAT-04_expected: A supported device emits one cue when inside the threshold; repeated updates do not repeat it within that alert state.
bsa_UAT-05_scenario: Use station selection and trip views at phone/tablet widths and with a keyboard.
bsa_UAT-05_expected: Content remains readable and core actions are reachable. Test on actual devices before claiming usability.
bsa_UAT-06_scenario: Simulate an unavailable feed, a healthy empty feed, stale data, and a fallback route.
bsa_UAT-06_expected: Proposed: present distinct states and estimate labels. Current aggregation is a known gap; do not mark this passed.
bsa_edge1_body: Manual station selection remains available; live location cannot be assumed. Device denial is exposed by the geolocation hook.
bsa_edge2_body: Current aggregation can hide failure. Proposed: separate no vehicles, unavailable service, and partial data; give a recovery action.
bsa_edge3_body: A straight-line fallback exists. Proposed: clearly mark the estimate and avoid implying a verified scheduled connection.
bsa_edge4_body: Trip loading catches storage errors; saving writes directly. Proposed: guard writes and explain that persistence is unavailable.
bsa_edge5_body: Planner returns no plans. Proposed: give a specific reason rather than reusing only the initial search prompt.
bsa_decision1_title: Fetch public live bus data in the browser.
bsa_decision1_why: Source comments explain that public CORS support lets live vehicles work on static hosting without server functions.
bsa_decision1_alternative: Route every feed through an application proxy.
bsa_decision1_tradeoff: Fewer runtime server dependencies, but the client now owns protobuf parsing, provider compatibility, and failure presentation.
bsa_decision2_title: Keep an active trip in localStorage.
bsa_decision2_why: Allows the route-selection and trip pages to share the chosen plan without mandatory cloud storage.
bsa_decision2_alternative: Persist every active trip through a backend.
bsa_decision2_tradeoff: Simple local continuity; device-specific state, storage failures, and no automatic cross-device sync.
bsa_decision3_title: Offer an estimated fallback when graph planning fails.
bsa_decision3_why: Source explicitly aims to return something for disconnected stations or bus endpoints.
bsa_decision3_alternative: Return no route with an explicit unsupported message.
bsa_decision3_tradeoff: Broader apparent coverage trades off itinerary confidence. Clear approximation labels should be a release condition.
bsa_risk1_impact: Outages or old positions can mislead a journey decision.
bsa_risk1_mitigation: Preserve feed status, show timestamps, and define a freshness policy before implementation.
bsa_risk2_impact: Model estimates are not a fare guarantee or timetable commitment.
bsa_risk2_mitigation: Label estimates; compare representative trips with operator information.
bsa_risk3_impact: GPS drift, battery limits, or unsupported vibration can affect cues.
bsa_risk3_mitigation: Test real devices; retain manual selection and communicate permission limits.
bsa_risk4_impact: Account history depends on deployed schema, auth, and access policies.
bsa_risk4_mitigation: Audit deployed policies separately; test signed-out and cross-account access before making security claims.
bsa_value1_output: Candidate cards with estimates and transfer counts.
bsa_value1_value: Potential usefulness of one planning experience; validate comprehension with commuters.
bsa_value2_output: Saved route, destination view, and GPS-dependent cues.
bsa_value2_outcome: Less need to remember an unfamiliar stop.
bsa_value2_value: Potential confidence while travelling; validate device reliability and perceived usefulness.
bsa_value3_output: Requirements, acceptance criteria, source references, and UAT designs.
bsa_value3_outcome: Make scope and unverified assumptions reviewable.
bsa_value3_value: A clearer basis for deciding what to validate next.
bsa_future1_body: Preserve partial-feed errors and freshness; show unavailable versus empty results. User value: honest journey confidence. Technical consideration: retain adapter metadata through aggregation.
bsa_future2_body: Expose fallback provenance in route cards. User value: avoid mistaking an approximation for a verified connection. Technical consideration: carry route provenance through planner output.
bsa_future3_body: Observe representative commuters comparing routes, then execute UAT on real devices. Product value: evidence for prioritization; define success criteria before collecting results.
bsa_future4_body: Validate demand for crowding reports before building submission. Product value: potentially richer journey context. Technical consideration: moderation, permissions, expiry, and abuse handling.
bsa_live_value: Add available bus context to a decision (expected).
bsa_hotel_constraints: Static HTML/CSS/JavaScript diploma team project. Preserve clear access to rooms, events, and FAQs across screen sizes.
bsa_hotel_solution: Organize hotel information into linked pages and consistent navigation. The delivered output is an information website.
bsa_hotel_contribution: Frontend contribution within a team project; existing page screenshots and the published site document the interface work.
bsa_hotel_verification: Proposed: given a visitor starts on the home page, when they choose Events or FAQs, then the correct page opens and navigation remains usable at phone width. These checks are not recorded as executed.
bsa_hotel_value: Expected value: make hotel information easier to find. No booking conversion or enquiry-delivery result is claimed for this static project.
bsa_cinema_constraints: PHP / JavaScript / CSS with XAMPP. Customer and administrator workflows need a clear boundary; deployed access-control behavior has not been audited here.
bsa_cinema_solution: Connect customer registration/login and administration in a cinema management project, supported by the existing forms and import-script assets.
bsa_cinema_contribution: Independent implementation documented in the existing portfolio, with customer-facing and administrative interfaces.
bsa_cinema_verification: Proposed: given a required registration field is empty, when the form is submitted, then validation should prevent an incomplete record. Separately test valid login and unauthorized admin access; no pass result is claimed.
bsa_cinema_value: Expected value: connect related customer and admin tasks in one system. Learning: UI completion must be checked against permissions, data integrity, and failure paths.
